tagline: Visual bookmark manager for saving, tagging, and searching links.
verdictSummary: A personal bookmark manager — save via a bookmarklet, tag freely, full-text search across saved pages — is a genuinely tractable weekend-scale build, and one of the cleanest yes entries here: bookmarking is a well-understood problem with mature open-source prior art already.
coreLoopDIY: A bookmarklet that saves a page's URL and metadata, stores the readable article text for search, and supports free-form tagging with full-text search across everything saved.
whyPeopleStillPay: Bookmarks are boring right up until search, mobile access, and extension reliability actually matter — people pay so all three just work without maintenance.
notes: A strong yes with real, mature prior art — this is a well-solved personal-tooling problem.
prompt:
Build a personal bookmark manager: a bookmarklet (or simple browser action) that sends the current page's URL to a save endpoint, which fetches the page, extracts the title, description, and preview image, and stores the readable article text (using a library like Mozilla's Readability) so search actually finds content, not just titles. Support free-form tags on each bookmark with tag autocomplete from what you've already used, plus an optional note. Build full-text search across title, note, and archived article text, filterable by tag, newest first. Run a periodic check that re-visits saved links and flags ones that now 404. Support importing a standard browser bookmarks export on day one, and exporting everything back out (JSON or CSV) so nothing is ever trapped.

Do not build a mobile app or full visual page-snapshot archiving — the extracted article text is the archive here, not a screenshot of the page, and that's a deliberate simplification, not an oversight. No shared team collections either; this is a personal tool.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Raindrop.io bookmarks?
faq.a: Yes — Raindrop exports a standard bookmarks HTML file, and importing that format on first run is exactly what this build expects.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The list and search are usable from a phone browser, but there's no native mobile app and no share-sheet integration for quickly saving a link from another app.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a database, typically a few dollars a month — the whole archive is a single database file, so storage costs stay small even with years of bookmarks.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Saving from anywhere instantly. Raindrop's polished mobile apps and share-sheet integration make saving a link a one-tap reflex; this build's bookmarklet works, but it's a more deliberate, desktop-first action.
